title: Unified SLI contract generator and failover crediting workflow
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Purpose: produce a repeatable way to derive per-endpoint and per-model SLI contracts from observed workload profiles and to encode a cross-region error-budget crediting workflow that integrates with circuit breakers and automated load-shedding.

Background: We have many ad-hoc SLO definitions across endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings) and for model variants. This creates operational friction during incidents and rollouts because engineers manually decide which variants to shed or which regions to borrow capacity from. The goal of this ticket is to implement a tooling + policy artifact (SLI contract generator) that: (1) ingests a workload profile (latency distribution, token lengths, request QPS, success/error taxonomy), (2) emits candidate SLIs and suggested thresholds (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokenized success rate, correctness/quality evaluation buckets), and (3) produces an error-budget crediting plan for multi-region failover and variant fallback.

Scope:
- Define canonical SLI primitives and measurement signals (latency quantiles, availability, model-quality score tied to promptset eval, tokenized error rate).
- Implement a CLI service that accepts a workload sample (ndjson of request traces) and returns suggested SLI contracts with rationales (why p95 vs p99, expected budget burn under load).
- Design error-budget escrow rules: pre-funded credits for short bursts, borrowing rules between regions, and credit repayment hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
- Hook credit signals into the circuit-breaker orchestrator: when region A burns >X% of its budget in Y minutes, automatically begin controlled failover to region B up to the escrow amount, and open circuit to low-priority variants.
- Define load-shedding runbook that favors cost-preserving degradations: (1) prefix/KV cache warming, (2) variant fallback (quantized/cheaper model), (3) degrade response fidelity (truncate generations with guided token limits), (4) hard reject for unauthenticated/bulk inferencing routes.
- Provide observability: per-contract burn dashboards, event timeline for credit transfers, and audit log entries for automated failovers.

Non-goals: full UI in Console, full enforcement across Dedicated private clusters (initially limited to hosted runtime and Dedicated orchestration controller).

Acceptance criteria:
- New SLI primitive catalog documented and approved by Reliability and API teams.
- CLI generator prototype that ingests a 24h trace and outputs at least three alternative contracts with simulated burn curves.
- Credit escrow policy doc with numeric examples and hysteresis parameters (cooldown windows, repayment caps).
- Playbook that maps credit events to circuit-breaker actions and load-shedding sequences.
- Integration tests that simulate a regional surge and show automated credit transfer + graceful degradation without violating higher-priority SLOs beyond defined thresholds.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://company.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/RI/pages/SLI-Contract-Generator-draft
- Trace sample: gs://redwood-inference-traces/slo-generator/24h-sample.ndjson
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sli-contract-generator (WIP branch: eng/ENG-420777)
